items.finding: Rival theory not discussed: Natural / ancient background resistome hypothesis

items.finding: Rival theory not discussed: Sink-versus-source / clinical clonal expansion hypothesis

items.finding: Rival theory not discussed: Fitness-cost and DNA-persistence / viability-decay hypothesis
items.evidence: Rivals risk interpretation from molecular detection: culture is gold standard for MIC/MBC but review relies heavily on molecular detection; extracellular DNA persistence after treatment means PCR/qPCR detection can overstate viable ARB transmission, with plasmid carriage decaying without continued selection.

missing_theories.name: Horizontal gene transfer / mobilome ecology theory
missing_theories.why: Manuscript reports high prevalence/diversity and co-occurrence of blaCTX-M, blaTEM, blaOXA, blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM etc. across wastewater/river/WWTP and invokes plasmids, transposons, integrons descriptively, but lacks explanatory theory for transfer rate, host-range, persistence and expression needed to link DNA detection frequency to active dissemination risk.

missing_theories.name: Selection pressure and co-selection theory
missing_theories.why: Core claim that WWTPs act as reservoirs and amplification points driven by interconnected factors and that conventional treatment cannot eliminate ARB/ARGs/residues requires theory linking sub-MIC antibiotics, metals, biocides and disinfectants to selection/co-selection; without it enrichment cannot be distinguished from survival/detection bias noted in Limitations heterogeneity.

missing_theories.name: Environmental fate-transport and quantitative microbial risk assessment framework
missing_theories.why: Claims that reservoirs contaminate irrigation/drinking water carrying genes back to humans/animals and that tracking variants clarifies transmission imply exposure and health risk, but no dose-response, decay, persistence/expression or horizontal-transfer probability framework is used to move from gene frequency (65.28% blaCTX-M etc.) to public-health risk; Conclusions call for persistence/expression/HGT studies.

rival_theories.name: Natural / ancient background resistome hypothesis
rival_theories.why: Rivals wastewater-as-driver/vector claim: many described families have environmental/chromosomal origins noted on p.10 (e.g., blaSFO, blaSME, blaCfxA, blaAmpC) and ARGs occur in soil/surface/drinking water, so high diversity could reflect natural background rather than wastewater propagation.

rival_theories.name: Sink-versus-source / clinical clonal expansion hypothesis
rival_theories.why: Rivals environment-to-human transmission chain: geographic patterns (China/India/USA/Brazil, Brazil blaKPC exception) and clinical relevance of blaCTX-M/KPC/NDM/VIM could be driven primarily by human/veterinary antibiotic use and expansion of successful clones with environment as passive sink where WWTPs still reduce viable loads despite residual DNA.

rival_theories.name: Fitness-cost and DNA-persistence / viability-decay hypothesis
rival_theories.why: Rivals risk interpretation from molecular detection: culture is gold standard for MIC/MBC but review relies heavily on molecular detection; extracellular DNA persistence after treatment means PCR/qPCR detection can overstate viable ARB transmission, with plasmid carriage decaying without continued selection.

fields.name: Environmental Microbiology / Antimicrobial Resistance Ecology
fields.evidence: high prevalence and diversity of β-lactamase genes in different environments; blaCTX-M 65.28%, blaTEM 60.24%, blaOXA 50.74%, blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaGES, blaIMP; AmpC genes blaAmpC, blaCMY, blaCIT, blaDHA; wastewater, river water and WWTP samples accounted for ~71% of samples; ARGs in soil, wastewater, surface water, drinking water

fields.name: Water Science / Environmental Engineering and Wastewater Treatment
fields.evidence: WWTPs act as key reservoirs and amplification points for ARB/ARGs; conventional treatment cannot eliminate ARGs; WWTPs designed for organics/nitrates/phosphates but not ARGs; removal technologies: Photo-Fenton 99.99% E. coli, UV 254nm 0.2-1.4 log, chlorination, ozonation, electrochemical, constructed wetlands; sludge disposal linked to ARG enrichment

fields.name: Public Health / One Health and Infectious Disease Epidemiology
fields.evidence: AMR silent pandemic, MDR bacteria, WHO Gram-negative resistant to 3rd-gen cephalosporins and carbapenems; One Health framework treats human, animal and environmental health as interconnected; plasmids/transposons/integrons spread across clinical, veterinary, environmental compartments; agricultural runoff, hospital effluents, irrigation/drinking water transmission; integrated surveillance needed

fields.name: Clinical Microbiology / Molecular Bacteriology of Beta-lactamases
fields.evidence: ESBL and carbapenemase determinants blaCTX-M, blaSHV, blaTEM, blaKPC, blaNDM, blaOXA, blaVIM; narrow-spectrum blaPSE, blaCARB, blaROB, blaZ, blaCfxA, blaSME, blaNPS; culture-based MIC/MBC gold standard plus molecular detection; references on CTX-M, SHV, NDM, OXA, GES, AmpC, VEB, SFO, CARB, ROB literature
